newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech govt plans to limit banks' equity exposure. [CORRECTED 15:45 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Czech govt plans to limit banks' equity exposure. [CORRECTED 15:45 GMT]

text.p: The Czech government approved a draft proposal on Wednesday which would limit the amount of shares banks could hold in any single company to 15 percent of the bank's basic capital, Finance Minister Ivan Pilip said. (Corrects basis for calculating equity exposure from "15 percent of the company's basic capital" to 15 percent of the bank's basic capital")

Speaking at a news conference during a cabinet meeting at a government chateau east of Prague, Pilip said the plan would also limit banks' consolidated exposure to equity in companies to 60 percent of capital. The amendments to the banking act, must still be approved by parliament.
"The proposal says the limit of participation of the bank in companies is 60 percent of the (consolidated) capital of the bank and 15 percent of the bank capital in one company," Pilip said.
He said that the entire holdings of the banks, including shares held by subsidiary investment companies and funds managed by those subsidiaries, would be included in the exposure calculation.
The Czech capital markets have been criticised for the heavy participation of banks and investment funds managed by the banks in equity holdings.
In a package of economic measures released in April, the government said it was committed to creating more transparency in the relationship between banks and companies.
